Dispatch's own functions (`buildAssignment`, `compileDispatchPlan`, `decideExecutorCli`, `executeExecutorCli`, `executeAssignment`, the assignment policy) now refuse a `work`/`workItem` input with "takes no Work item" instead of silently ignoring it, and name the `--work` selector `workId`.
- When the config sets a rigor on a `<domain>:review` capability, a declared assignment of that domain (including a Work driver step) gets that floor: the policy reads the domain the assignment carries. It only ever raises rigor.
- Dispatch no longer imports a domain's contract harness (`domains/<d>/harness/enrich-and-validate-contract.mjs`) by a computed path; only the Work layer loads it, for a caller to hand in.
- The runner loop (`fgos-runner`) and the fan-out batch run each worker as one Unit run, through the same boundary as `fgos run`: the worker runs confined and never commits, and the runner commits what it left. The item's log names the Unit run (`unitRunId`) and where its output is captured instead of teeing the worker's output live, and the `executor.dispatch` event carries `unitRunId`. Commit subjects become `chore(work-<id>-<step>): <the worker's claim summary>`.
- A runner loop step asks for its capability as `<domain>:<verb>` (for example `coding:discover`), the name its Workflow uses; a config that only declares the bare verb still serves it.
- An item no executor can run (its capability has no usable pool) parks as `no-executor`, with the pool to configure in the message, instead of stopping the runner. Every candidate at its provider limit parks the item as `provider-limit`. A worker round that fails after writing files is `worker-failed`: retried, and its uncommitted files are never verified as if they were on the branch.
- A runner loop round that stopped over its own half-done writes, or whose runner commit failed, keeps its worktree; the item's next attempt resumes the same Unit run there, committing again without running the agent a second time.
- Driver steps of a work item (`fgos plan <id> --validate`, and the runner loop's validate-plan, review and scout operations) run as Units through the same door as `fgos run`. Their worker is confined, so a read-only operation can no longer write to the checkout. A step stops instead of advancing when its runner commit failed. Results recorded before this change are still read.
- A validate-plan verdict is bound to the bytes of `plan.md`, keyed by its path inside the checkout. A plan validated in the item worktree and merged byte for byte is therefore not validated again, and any edit after validation still forces a new one.
- Driver steps need a confinement backend (bwrap). Without one, the step stops with `unit-refused-posture-unavailable` instead of running unconfined.
- An item with `rigor: low` that runs as a Unit uses the `standard` tier.
- Resuming a unit run uses the pattern it started with; a pattern passed on resume is ignored.
- A runner commit whose worker left no summary is named after the goal line of the unit's objective instead of `producer changes`. A long commit subject is cut at a sentence or word boundary instead of ending in `...`.
- `fgos run` (and a Workflow unit) commits only files inside the Unit's `writes`. Files outside it are left in place and reported in `commit.outOfScope`; files you were already editing inside the scope are left as they are (`preExistingInScope`).
- The runner refuses to start a writing Unit while the index already holds staged changes (`foreign-staged-index`); unstage or commit them and run again.
- Runner commits use a conventional subject: the first line of the worker's `summary`, or `chore(<unitId>): …` when that is not conventional.
- Unit `writes` are normalized to one spelling and `.`, absolute paths, `..` and pathspec magic `:` are refused; only `*` and `**` are globs.
- A Workflow definition's `writes` must be a list: an empty `writes:` in YAML (null) or any other non-list value is refused instead of silently becoming `[]`.
- A writing seat of a unit run is told its write scope, that the runner (not the agent) commits, that the commit subject comes from the first line of `summary`, and to declare `needsWrites` when it needs a path outside the scope.
- A unit run's evidence marks files inside the declared `writes` (`coverageMatched`) and warns about files outside them.
- A `persona` in a workflow unit template travels on the Unit (provenance `unit`) instead of becoming an `origin: workflow` override.
- A writing workflow unit that depends on another writing unit now starts from that unit's branch instead of HEAD; `workflow status` lists `writeBranches`.
- A writing unit that changed files outside its `writes` ends as `findings`; an integrate step that meets such a unit fails and merges nothing (it used to skip it silently).
- A writing unit that cannot get a worktree of its own now fails instead of running in the shared checkout.
- The verb manifest's `schema_version` is `3.0`: a verb with sub-verbs keeps only `sub` in its verb-level `parameters`, and each sub-verb's flags are under `subcommands.<sub>.parameters`.
- `fgos --help` refuses an unknown verb, sub-verb, extra word or option with exit 4 instead of ignoring it. It still accepts `--dir`, which the `fgos` shell function appends.
- The `fgos run` and `fgos workflow` help say which door to use: one task → `fgos run "<prompt>"`; planned work → `fgos workflow start <preset>|--units <file>`.
- A fresh checkout, a linked worktree and `fgos setup` no longer need `npm install`: fgOS has no npm runtime dependency now. Its YAML parser (js-yaml) ships inside the source tree and every YAML read goes through one wrapper, `src/util/yaml.mjs`, so `fgos doctor` check `dependencies-installed` passes with "no runtime dependencies declared" and the workflow tests load without `node_modules`.
- Agent definitions (`fgos/agents`, `domains/*/agents`, `core/agents`) and project or domain workflow files must be valid YAML. `fgos doctor` names a file that is not, with its line and column, in the checks `agent-claims-resolve`, `agent-type-names-unique`, `workflow-capabilities-configured`, `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` and `blind-steps-use-proven-pools`; a seat that names such a definition is refused, and the agent roster skips it with one warning line on stderr. A definition indented as a whole now reads as a mapping and seats; a numeric `name: 123` reads as "123".
- `fgos doctor` checks `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` and `blind-steps-use-proven-pools` now evaluate in a copy without dependencies instead of passing with "not evaluated", so a project can see new failures there. A workflow that cannot be parsed fails those checks and `workflow-capabilities-configured` by name, but no longer hides their results for the other workflows. A problem path is prefixed `package:` or `project:` when both trees are scanned, and a file that cannot be read is reported as such rather than as unparsable.
- A persona whose list item or value reads as a mapping (an unquoted `": "`, for example `- Escalate when: budget exceeded`) is refused with its path by `fgos agents`, `fgos doctor` and persona resolution, instead of the text being dropped silently. Pinned text from an earlier run with that shape still renders as it was pinned.
- A workspace persona that cannot be parsed or has the wrong shape refuses `fgos run` and workflow unit runs with the named problem; before, the run fell back to the core persona of the same name or to no persona text.
- A YAML file whose aliases expand past 100000 values, or that references itself, is rejected with a message naming the file.
- `fgos doctor` check `agent-type-names-unique` reports problems as `<file>: <problem>`, like the other checks. The dispatch warning `agent roster: …` for a bad agent file prints once per process instead of on every lookup.
- `fgos doctor` check `domain-registry-compiled` now also reports a `compiled.json` that is stale against its YAML and domain YAML that cannot be parsed; `npm run build:domains` regenerates it.
- Persona text rendered into a worker prompt now comes from the parsed agent file: a block-scalar value shows in full, an inline `# comment` is stripped and a number is normalised (`1e3` shows as `1000`). A persona file that cannot be parsed renders one `could not be parsed` line instead of silently dropping its section; a run pinned by an earlier release resumes with the persona text it was pinned with.
- The doctor check for orphaned confinement resources skips attempt homes (they belong to adopt) and its fix goes through the same sweep as the other cleanup call sites; it never removes an attempt home.

### Removed
- The controller's herdr round: the polling loop, its deadline and idle handling, the settle and pane-closing code, the launcher script and its process checks, `herdr-reconcile`, the liveness probe and `herdr-diagnosis.json`, and the pane, endpoint and launch-time fields of the home ownership marker. A home written with a pane binding by an older release is no longer swept: clean it with that release before activating this one.

- The Node run supervisor (`detached-run-supervisor.mjs`), its IPC channel to the controller and its pane-less home binding (`bindConfinedHomesToSupervisor`), the old cli-spawn reconciler (`reconcile-cli-spawn.mjs`), the `legacySpawn` option and the `protected/supervisor-binding` and `protected/adapter-receipts` files of cli-spawn runs. Runs started before this release keep their files and are read as `legacy-run`.
- `fgos doctor` check `provider-capacity-lock-stale`: the provider-capacity state is no longer guarded by a lock file a dead process can leave behind.
- `fgos-runner --config <path>`: the runner and its workers always use the repo's own `.fgos/config.json`.
- `fgos dispatch execute` is gone, together with its `--contract` and `--assignment` forms and the `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute` alias. Run one task with `fgos run "<prompt>" --provider <executor>` (`--provider` takes an agent executor; a `kind: "tool"` executor is called directly) (add `--writes <paths> --worktree <linked-worktree>` for work that changes files; the runner commits them), or a Unit file with `fgos run --unit <file>`; planned work goes through `fgos workflow start`. Calling the old door returns an error naming the replacement, and the dispatch-decide hook's BLOCKED message names the same `fgos run` form.
- `fgos dispatch log` is gone: every `fgos run` already records its Unit, binding, results and commit under `.fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/`.
- `dispatch fanout-batch` is gone. Fanout runs from `node src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs "<ids>" [--has-live-task-access]`, with the same output keys (`fired`, `mechanismChanged`, `unavailable`, `deferred`, and `slotsFull: true` when no slot is free).
- `decide --work` runs only as `fgos dispatch decide --work <id>`; `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs decide --work` is refused with a pointer to it.
- `AGENTS.md` and every skill render no longer teach the removed doors. Other projects keep their old rendered skills until they activate a release that carries this change and run `fgos setup`.
- The `yaml` npm dependency, the hand-written YAML readers in the doctor checks and the persona renderer, and the "not evaluated: yaml package not installed" branches. `fgos doctor` no longer warns about multi-line persona markers because they now render.

### Fixed
- `fgos dispatch recover` no longer parks an orphaned attempt only because `outbox/result-N.json` exists, and a unit whose only attempt the legacy sweep settled no longer reads `running`.
- Attempts left `running` with no holder are cleaned up: new ones through adopt (`run-attempts-stuck`), runs from before the run supervisor through `legacy-attempts-stuck`.
- The gate of a supervised attempt can read its envelope and run when the run directory or the host binary lives under `/tmp`: the sandbox mounts its own `/tmp`, so both are now bound back in place. Before, such a run ended `gate-lost` with `envelope unreadable`.
- A `FGOS_HOST_BIN` that names a file that cannot be run is now an error everywhere the host is looked up; it no longer falls back to the activated release.
- A borrowed lock no longer kills unrelated child processes of the lock holder: cleanup kills the borrowed command, its process group and any escaped descendant that still holds the lock, and waits for the holder’s other children that are between fork and exec (Rust and Node use the same rule). A borrow also refuses a lock whose file was replaced (`lock-resource-replaced`).
- Process containment no longer reports `spawn-failed` when a short command exits before its identity is read; a gate that already exited counts as an empty domain.
- A gemini worker now runs the model its tier asks for. Since gemini moved to omp, the omp invocations passed no `--model`, so every tier ran the profile default (`gemini-3.8-flash`); a frontier task now runs `gemini-4-argon`.
- `fgos take`, `fgos list` and every other verb that reads active claims no longer spawn one git process per open claim; with 60 open claims a `take` drops from about 270 child processes and 1.7 s to 21 processes and 0.26 s.

- The advance and recovery locks no longer stay stuck when their holder dies while creating the lock file; both now live under the run's `locks/` directory.
- The `fgos run --resume` guard no longer treats a dispatch lock it cannot read as free.
- `fgos dispatch reconcile` help, usage errors and docs no longer advertise the retired `clear-assignment-claim` action (and its `--assignment` flag); the planner already refused it, so the supported actions are `clear-cwd-lock`, `collect-result` and `repair-projection`.
- The confinement orphan reaper no longer deletes the private home (and the login copy in it) of a worker that is still running when the process that launched it dies. A confined herdr round now records its pane, the herdr socket its client used, its own pid and start time and the time of binding in the home's ownership marker before the worker starts (a round that cannot record this closes its pane and fails), and a cli-spawn round records its detached run supervisor the same way. A home whose recorded process is alive is kept for its run timeout plus launch and settle grace from that moment, whatever herdr answers; a home bound to a pane that never received a worker is removed and the empty pane closed. Panes of default-session rounds can now be asked about, and the reaper re-reads the marker before removing a home, skipping one that changed since it decided.
- `fgos run --provider <executor>` (a bare executor id in a Unit's `prefer`) inside herdr now binds the executor's herdr invocation, as a capability pool does, instead of the confined cli invocation posture approval had filled in (transport source `unit-prefer-pinned-invocation`). A `prefer` entry that names an invocation, or an override's invocation, still keeps it.
- Releasing another writer's runtime claim is now auditable after the claim file is gone: `fgos unclaim` appends a `decision` event (`source: unclaim`, `kind: engine`) with `admin: {reason, ownerWriterId, releasedByWriterId, claimId}`, and the stale-claim reclaim in `pick` adds the same `admin` field to the decision it already wrote. A writer releasing its own claim records nothing new.
- `fgos run --rigor low` (and a Unit's `rigor: low`) now binds the nano tier when the capability declares no `rigor` floor; bind used to treat the implicit `standard` as a floor, so a low run on `execute` resolved `sonnet` instead of the `nano` model. A capability's own `rigor` still raises a lower Unit rigor.
- `/fgOS:terminal` and `/fgOS:terminal-close` act only on the caller's own live herdr pane. Before renaming or closing, they ask herdr for the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` and check that its shell is an ancestor of the caller; a dead pane or another session's pane (the id a shared `codex app-server` daemon passes to every child) is refused with a one-line message on stderr and nothing is changed.
- `fgos dispatch probe-account` no longer removes a private home kept for a pane that is still open once that home is past its maximum age: the sweep it runs after closing its own panes asks herdr about every other pane exactly as the regular sweep does, instead of treating them as unanswerable.
- A cli-spawn `fgos run` whose controlling process crashes or is killed mid-run no longer loses the worker: the detached run supervisor stops sending live output to the dead controller instead of crashing on the closed channel, so the worker keeps running, the deadline is still enforced, and the run's capture and receipt are still written.
- `fgos pick`/`take`, `fgos approve` (land) and `fgctl init` no longer wait up to 3 minutes after every commit on the main checkout, including the committing session's own. The fgOS pre-commit hook no longer writes `.fgos/main-checkout.lock`; it leaves a commit-activity beacon in `.fgos/runtime/main-checkout-activity.json` (writer, time and a `windowMs`, 20 s by default or `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`) that only the hook reads, to refuse another session's commit inside that window. `fgos lock-status` reports the beacon as `activity`, and `fgos return`/`cleanup`/`compound` clear the session's own beacon instead of the lock. The hook still refuses a commit, without waiting, while an fgOS claim, checkpoint or land holds the lock.
- Every holder of `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` or a merge slot now records its own `ttlMs` (the dispatch worktree lock is a kernel lock with no ttl, see above), and a contender judges the record by that ttl instead of its own (a dispatch with a longer timeout no longer outwaits a shorter holder, and a short contender no longer takes a longer holder's lock). A record left by an older release counts for 20 s when it is a session id (old hook) and 3 minutes when it is a pid.
- The `.fgos` events checkpoint that runs during `fgos approve` under a merge slot now holds `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` for its whole add, commit and reset, so it can no longer interleave with a land on the main checkout; when a land holds the lock the checkpoint is skipped until the next call. Claim and a merge without a slot reuse the lock they already hold.
- A lock record with a `v` field (even one that also has `pid` and `ts`), or a lock protocol marker (`.fgos/runtime/locks/<lock>/protocol.json`) naming any protocol other than 1, is refused with "upgrade fgOS" and is never reclaimed, released, renewed or overwritten by this release. The marker is checked before anything else, so the pre-commit hook, `fgos lock-status`, `fgos unlock`, the claim self-heal and `fgctl init` all refuse even when the lock file itself is absent or corrupt; `fgos unlock` never reports `cleared` there. Do not downgrade below this release once a newer lock protocol is in use.
- A native `fgos` verb that takes no stdin (for example `fgos convention path ...`) no longer waits for an inherited stdin to close: it hung under a heredoc, an agent Bash tool, or a pipe whose writer stays open. Only `metrics ping`, `metrics eval record`, and `friction record --detail-stdin` read stdin.
- A headless round that stops because the provider account used up its quota (codex "You've hit your usage limit") now settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota` instead of a generic non-zero exit, so a Workflow unit or `fgos run` moves to another account or candidate, and a leased account waits out the reset time the provider printed.
- A dispatch round is no longer refused because files changed in a shared checkout while it ran (`wrote-outside-workspace`, `read-only-mutation`, `mutated-dirty-before-files`). A before/after snapshot cannot tell the worker's writes from another session's, so the round is accepted and the paths are reported in its result as `warnings` (`stray-write-correlated`, `read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`) and on stderr. A write proven to be the run's own would still be refused; nothing proves one yet.
- An Assignment run's `result.json` now names the sandbox it really ran under in `confinement` (`bwrap`), read from the launch the Confinement Authority prepared or the dispatch's enforced attestation; it was always `null` before, even for sandboxed seats.
- A Work item stopped on a read-only round whose checkout changed while it ran now says so: the round is accepted with its `warnings`, and the driver stops with `assignment-<operation>-correlated-mutation` (at planning `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`) instead of a generic failed or no-evidence reason. A round launched through the executor CLI door now keeps that door's `stray-write-correlated` warning in its `result.json` instead of only printing it.
- `fgos run --resume` is refused while a live dispatch still holds the worktree's lock, so a second worker is never started in the same worktree; the old guard read a lock name no dispatch writes and never refused.
- A Unit's `persona` is resolved and its text pinned when the unit run starts, so a persona defined only in the workspace (`fgos/agents/`) is rendered with its definition instead of its bare name.
- A help token never runs the verb: `fgos init --json -h` created a store and `fgos session start --json -h` created a worktree, because the help token was read as the previous flag's value; through the Rust host, `fgos version --help` ran `version` and `fgos metrics runs --help` ran `runs`.
- Manifest entries now match what the CLI reads: `merge next` lists the flags it forwards to approve/sync-root, `workflow start --stance-options`, `workflow operations --step` (was `--stage`), `tool --config`, `tool check --name` (was a positional), `dispatch decide --assignment`, `run record --result`. AGENTS.md and the dispatch fallback skill say `decide --work <id> [--stage <stage>]` (was `--step`).

### Security

- The runner commit no longer trusts a worktree's `.git` file, a relative hooks path or fsmonitor: its git runs against the main repository's gitdir with the caller's `GIT_*` variables dropped, and a worktree outside the main repository is refused.

## [v0.2.0-rc.5] - 2026-10-14

### Added

- `fgos dispatch execute <executor> --for <capability>` names the kind of work a dispatch does; the capability, not the executor, sets whether it may change files. `execute <agent>` without `--for` is now refused before spawning with the choices listed, and this door carries writing work only: read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `"writes": []` (`fgos workflow start --units <file>`); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider but enforces read-only by instruction only, without a sandbox. `--timeout-ms` and `--idle-timeout-ms` override the configured timeouts for one call.
- A `for` list on an agent executor is now ignored (it used to set the posture of every dispatch to that executor); `for` keeps its meaning on `kind: "tool"` executors. `fgos doctor` names each leftover under `executor-profile-warnings` so it can be removed.
- `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider <provider> --account <account>` starts every CLI configured for one provider account (Codex, pi, omp) at the same moment through the same door a read-only dispatch uses (sandbox, the account's login copied into a private home, a herdr pane for pane invocations) with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI whether it answered or stopped at a trust prompt, a dead login, a quota, the sandbox or a timeout, with the line that shows it and the run and pane it used, plus whether the fault looks like the account's or one CLI's. It closes the panes it opened. It only diagnoses: it picks and schedules nothing.
- A provider account in `~/.fgos/config.json` (`runner.providers.<provider>.accounts.<id>`) can declare one login store per CLI with `credentialSources: { codex: {...}, pi: {...} }` instead of the single `credentialSource`, so one account can be used through Codex, pi or omp while each CLI keeps its own login. A confined launch gets the store of the CLI it actually runs (copied into its private home, renewed and written back to that store, folder trust read from it); a launch pinned to one CLI only leases an account that has a store for it, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts. Quota, locks and quarantine stay per account. `credentialSource` keeps working unchanged. An older fgos release refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources`, so update fgos before adding it.

### Changed

- `fgos run` gives a unit's agent to the run supervisor instead of running it as a child of the controller: the controller takes the attempt lock (and the cwd lease when the agent writes), starts `fgos internal supervise` detached and from then on only reads progress and the result, so killing or losing the controller no longer loses the run. Live output (`onChunk`) is read from the capture files. A run resumed after a controller crash asks the adopt door about its attempt and never starts a second agent over it.
- `fgos dispatch reconcile <runDir>` asks the adopt door and prints its answer (`running`, `being-adopted`, `adopted`, `closed`, `held`, `legacy-run`); a run from before the run supervisor answers `legacy-run`. The `--control-epoch` and `--control-token` flags are gone.
- Confined Codex accounts now fail closed when `auth.json` is a symlink that resolves outside the Codex home, or when the configured `home` is a relative path; the dispatch stops before the worker starts. Both used to be accepted (the symlink was followed, a relative home was resolved against the working directory).

### Fixed

- A read-only dispatch (`execute --contract`, a read-only Workflow unit or pane) no longer tells the worker its write scope is "none" right beside the result files it must write. A Codex worker read that as a ban, answered the task, wrote no result file, and the round scored `no-evidence`. The prompt now says the work is read-only in the workspace and that the result files sit outside it and are still required.
- `fgos dispatch probe-account` no longer reports `cli-fault` for a healthy account because of its invocations that declare no sandbox. The probe confines every round, so those invocations always stop on `EROFS` in their own login directory; they are still listed, but the verdict now reads only the invocations that declare their own sandbox (each row says `inVerdict`), and reads `no-confined-cli` when there is none.
- `fgos doctor` check `confined-pane-accounts` now reads the provider account inventory from `~/.fgos/config.json` whatever directory doctor runs in; it used to be skipped silently outside a project with a config. An unreadable global config now fails the check, naming the error code and path only, and provider and account ids named like `constructor` are looked up as ordinary ids.
- `fgos doctor` check `credential-copies-retained` fails, naming the directory, on login copies of any age left in a store directory the account's layout no longer reads (after an account switches between one login store and one store per CLI, drops a CLI, or leaves the provider inventory); no dispatch applies them, so they are recovered by hand. They are no longer reported as applied by the next dispatch. - `fgos doctor`'s `task-specs-resolve` and `domain-workflow-operations-coverage` checks no longer fail in a plain target project that has no fgOS `domains/` or `core/` tree; they resolve the task-specs and agent files against the fgOS install they run from.
- A sandboxed headless (`cli-spawn`) worker is now told to write its result claim and report under the run's `worker-output/outbox`, the one run directory the sandbox leaves writable. The prompt and effective contract used to name the flat run directory, which is read-only there, so a worker that followed the prompt literally (deepseek through pi) failed with `EROFS` and landed no claim.
- A herdr agent stopped on a prompt only a person can answer (codex's "Trust this folder?" for a project it has no trust for) now ends the round as `blocked` instead of `execution-timeout`. The liveness ladder already concluded `blocked` and named the screen line, but settlement treated every failure carrying the worker-timeout error class as a timeout, so the run record said timeout/resource, the unit outcome was `execution-failure`, and the real repair was lost. The failure code is now `blocked`, the unit outcome `blocked`, and the message says to answer the prompt in the pane or grant trust for the project in the agent's own home.
- Empty per-dispatch directories under the confinement temp root (`/tmp/fgos-confinement/disp_*`) are now removed. They held nothing and carried no ownership marker, so the reaper skipped them and about 2000 had piled up, using inodes. The reaper removes an empty one once it is ten minutes old, and `fgos doctor` counts and `--fix` removes them.
- A herdr round no longer outlives its pane. When a pane is closed (or vanishes) herdr answers `pane_not_found` to the liveness read, which used to count as an unreadable read, so the round ran to its absolute ceiling; now consecutive `pane_not_found` answers end it as `died` within seconds, naming the pane. An unreachable, timed-out or unparseable herdr is still not evidence of death.
- A confined agent's status in herdr is now true. fgos used to report the state "working" for the pane when it launched the agent, which made fgos the pane's status authority: `agent get` stayed "working" for the whole round even when the agent had finished, stalled or stopped on a limit, and an earlier workaround read the screen detector's verdict first (two herdr calls per poll). Measured on herdr 0.9.1: claude, codex, agy and pi are recognised behind the bwrap wrapper on their own, and their status moves idle, working, done as they work. fgos now reports a state only for a process herdr cannot recognise as an agent (after a six second grace), and reads `agent get`, asking the detector only when the status is unknown. One herdr call per poll instead of two, and `agent wait` and `agent prompt --wait` work for confined panes.
- Each role of a Unit run now gets its own task. Every role used to be dispatched with the unit's objective, so a reviewer told to "replace the placeholder line" tried to replace it instead of checking the producer's work, and a panel synthesizer was told to "silently generate independent ideas". The `reviewed` and `panel` patterns now tell the reviewer, red-team and synthesizer what they are for (default texts live in `role-tasks.mjs` and can be replaced with `params.roleTasks`), hand the reviewer and red-team the producer's report, and, from round 2, list the previous round's findings for the producer (they were passed along but never reached it).
- A dispatch no longer leaves a background process behind. The codex CLI starts an `app-server-daemon` out of the private home it was given and keeps it running after the pane closes; removing the home deleted its files but not the process, so every codex dispatch leaked tens of megabytes (dozens of leftovers had piled up to about 2 GB). Removing a private home, or any confinement resource, now stops the processes that still run from inside it. Linux only, like the confinement it belongs to.
- A codex pane whose model is "at capacity" is now reported as a provider limit, so the round falls back to the next candidate executor instead of waiting out its ceiling. Two gaps were closed. The runner only knew a few generic limit phrases, so "Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model." was never recognised. And a pane that herdr keeps reporting as `working` (which counts as progress) was never read at all, so a parked agent ran the full fifteen minutes (seen in the mdview dogfood). The tail of a `working` agent's screen is now checked every 30 seconds for a line that starts with the CLI's own error marker and names the condition, and the same line must still be there a full interval later; ordinary text that merely mentions capacity or rate limits is left alone.
- The `glm` executors run the `pi` CLI through OpenRouter (model `z-ai/glm-5.2`) instead of the claude CLI behind a gateway. In a herdr pane the claude route stopped at "Please run /login, API Error: 401" every time, so a synthesizer bound to `glm-herdr` never produced anything. The API key is still only the `${GLM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY}` environment reference.
- A project set up with `fgctl init` can run `fgos workflow` (and every other verb that loads a dependency). The release tree used to ship the CLI without its `yaml` package, so these verbs failed with "Cannot find package 'yaml'" even though `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` passed. The tree now carries its production dependencies, a missing dependency fails the build, and the external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb.
- A herdr dispatch no longer deletes a folder-trust entry it did not write. A read-only run in the main checkout used to remove the entry you had vouched for when it settled, so every later Claude start in that folder (yours and the next dispatch) stopped at the trust dialog. Teardown now removes only the entry its own round seeded, for the claude, codex and agy trust stores alike.
- A `panel` synthesizer now receives its panelists' reports: the runner hands the results of earlier roles to the next role as context refs. Before, the synthesizer was dispatched with no context refs and judged without seeing the panel.
- A worker no longer commits on any path: the Work loop, the discovery sweep and `fanout-batch` stage and commit what the worker left in the item worktree (the same runner commit `fgos run` uses) before goal-check or `fgos return`; a clean tree is not an error, so a worker that still commits itself keeps working, and a commit that fails is routed as an infrastructure failure. The worker log records `commit runner | self | none`. The worker contract and prompt templates tell workers to edit files and stop, and the default `runner.executor` and this repo's `claude-cli`/`glm` invocations lose their `git add`/`git commit` `--allowedTools` grant (the earlier exception is superseded). `fgos doctor` (`invocation-git-write-grants`) warns about any executor or invocation in your own config that still grants it -- remove the grant from your `.fgos/config.json`.
- A `workspace-write` producer that stops on a provider limit now falls back to the next candidate like a read-only role does; the write gate follows the fallback chain the runner recorded in `unit.json` (each attempt now records `skipCandidateIndex` and `candidateIndex`) and still refuses a binding the runner did not record.
- Confined workers' private homes (which hold a copy of the account login) are created owner-only (0700, including the `fgos-confinement` root, the per-run directory and credential subdirectories), a Codex `auth.json` copy is 0600, and the home plus its run directory are removed when a run fails. The one exception: a failure that leaves its herdr pane open keeps the home for that pane (its path is on the error as `retainedPrivateHomes`); `fgos run`, the runner loop and `fgos doctor --fix` remove it once the pane is closed. A `/tmp/fgos-confinement` owned by another user is no longer reused (a per-uid root is used); `fgos doctor` flags a confinement root readable beyond its owner.
- Rewriting a provider trust store (`.claude.json`, agy `settings.json`, Codex `config.toml`) keeps the file's permission bits; a 0600 file no longer becomes group/world-readable.
- A `workspace-write` worker no longer writes git metadata at all: its own gitdir and the shared one are read-only in the sandbox (it could otherwise move any branch ref or overwrite objects of the whole repository). It writes files in its worktree; after a producer round passes, the runner commits them from outside the confinement (`git add -A` minus `.fgos/`, then `git commit`, the message is the agent's summary). A round that left nothing to commit makes no commit and the run record (`unit.json` bindings, `commit.status`) says `no-changes`; a commit that cannot be made fails the round. The effective execution contract no longer lists `git add`/`git commit` as allowed worker commands.
- `fgos workflow start` now returns at once with the run id and how to read progress (`fgos workflow status <id>`) while a detached process keeps running the workflow, instead of holding the caller for the whole run (and orphaning panes when wrapped in `timeout`). Pass `--foreground` to stay attached until the run completes, fails or parks.
- `fgos workflow answer` and `fgos workflow resume` return at once the same way (`answer` records the answer first); `--foreground` keeps them attached. A run that a live process is already advancing refuses a second advance with a clear message instead of racing it.
- `fgos workflow start` takes `--request <text>`; every unit gets the request and the output of the steps it depends on. A unit that is refused or fails now ends its step and the run as `failed` instead of being counted as passed.
- A reviewer or panelist now runs on a different provider family than the producer or its sibling panelists; with too few families the run is refused instead of repeating one.
- `fgos run` detects a live herdr session.
- `fgos run` now uses the transport `bind()` chose: inside a herdr session an executor with a herdr-spawn invocation runs in a pane (the run record `assignment.json` and `unit.json` state the transport and invocation), otherwise cli-spawn. A read-only or workspace-write posture wraps the agent inside the pane exactly as it does for cli-spawn, so herdr-spawn invocations now declare `confinement: { backend: "bwrap" }` (the repo config is updated; one without it stays on cli).
- One posture path: a read-only or workspace-write posture is resolved from the Unit run's binding into a confinement requirement and applied by the confinement driver for both cli-spawn and herdr-spawn; `canApplyPosture` now reflects whether the backend is configured and its executable exists, so a role whose invocation cannot be confined is refused as `posture-unavailable` (or another candidate is chosen) instead of running unconfined. When a capability's `prefer` entry names no invocation, `bind()` records the first plain cli invocation that can carry the posture (the one the posture check approved, not the executor's first cli invocation), so a headless `fgos run` uses it; an entry that names an invocation keeps it. The second, hand-built bwrap argument list in `confinement/policies.mjs` is removed.
- When an agent stops on a provider limit, the role moves to the next candidate of the capability's `prefer` list (a new pane under herdr; the limited pane stays open) and the move is recorded as `fallbackFrom`; with no candidate left the outcome stays `provider-limit`. A resumed run reuses the bindings recorded in `unit.json`.
- A confined agent in a herdr pane no longer loses its task: the brief is typed once the agent's prompt is up, and an unsent draft left in the prompt box is submitted with Enter (bounded, recorded as `briefSubmitKeyResent` in `visibility.json`). A claude REPL in a pane is also given its run directory as a working directory (`--add-dir`), so it does not stop on claude's own "read outside the working directories" prompt.
- The brief a reviewer or red-team reads in a herdr pane now says its claim needs `assessment.verdict` (it was only in the headless prompt, so a pane reviewer wrote a claim the runner refused as invalid).
- A confined agent in a herdr pane is now watched through herdr's screen detector instead of the status fgos reported at launch, which stayed "working" forever: a hung agent or one stopped on a provider limit is now noticed, so the provider-limit fallback can fire in a real pane.
- A herdr round with no `idleTimeoutMs` in the runner config now gets a 5-minute idle limit (no agent activity, ack or outbox file), so a stalled agent or a provider-limit screen is acted on instead of holding the pane to the 35-minute ceiling.
- The herdr client reads an agent's screen from herdr 0.9.1, which prints it as plain text instead of in the JSON envelope; before, every screen read failed silently, so a provider-limit screen was never matched and the reason a pane stalled was never quoted.
- The confined herdr launch no longer calls an honest launch an environment tamper because the shell rewrote `SHLVL` or `_`.
- The codex (openai), agy (gemini) and pi (xai) herdr invocations now run in a pane under the same bwrap posture as the claude ones. Each agent keeps its state in a private home (`resourceBindings` `private-home` -> `CODEX_HOME` / `HOME` / `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) provisioned from the leased provider account: the new `home-files` credential source in the machine-global `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` lists the files to copy, the real account directory stays read-only, and a missing file refuses the pane before launch. These invocations no longer take the prompt as an argument (the brief is typed once the agent is up) and codex no longer relies on `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (`-s danger-full-access -a never`, with bwrap enclosing it). Workspace trust is written to the private home, derived from the real account store; an agent herdr has no screen rule for is typed at only after its screen has drawn and held still. `fgos doctor` has a `confined-pane-accounts` check that names a pane whose account login would not reach it.
- `fgos setup` registers the capabilities of every shipped Workflow (marketing, architecture, business, delphi, group-cognition, nominal-group, coding) (`runner.capabilities.<domain>:<verb>`) so another project can run those Workflows; it only adds missing entries and keeps ones the project already tuned. The slots are description-only (no `prefer`): which executors serve a capability is the project's choice, and until it declares a `prefer` pool, on the exact name or on the bare verb, a headless run of that Workflow unit is refused. `bind()` now falls through to the bare-verb entry when the exact entry has no `prefer`, so a new slot never hides a project's own bare-verb pool. `fgos doctor` check `workflow-capabilities-configured` names any capability a Workflow uses that config lacks (failure) or declares without a `prefer` pool (warning).
- The panel synthesizer now runs on a different provider family than every panelist.
- A finished Workflow run (complete or failed) removes the worktrees of its integrated Units; a failed Unit's worktree stays for investigation and its path is recorded in the run event. A Unit counts as integrated when its branch is part of the integration target: the `target` an `integrate` step declares, else the remote's default branch, else the branch the main checkout is on — so a repository whose trunk is `master` or `trunk` is cleaned up too (the target used to be a literal `main`).
- A confined agent pane that is showing a dialog, or never reached its prompt, now fails the round at once (`worker-spawn-fail`, reason `agent_blocked` / `agent_not_ready`, with the line on screen) instead of being typed at; the brief used to answer the dialog and the round hung until the idle ceiling.
